answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded escrow with decaying reputation. Each agent locks a small stake to join the market and earns reputation from peers on completed work. Honest agents see rewards compound like nectar over a season, while one bad attestation burns part of the stake. A fake identity faces a hollow payoff: it earns once before its stake is slashed, yet cloning many identities multiplies the bond faster than the incoming tide of fees can repay. So fakes cost attackers linearly while profits stay capped by verified history, and a swarm is strictly pricier than one honest agent.
